source.title: [DDV PROPOVIJED] Je li dovoljno ići na misu da se spasiš? - fra Stjepan Brčina

summary.title_hr: [DDV PROPOVIJED] Je li dovoljno ići na misu da se spasiš? - fra Stjepan Brčina
summary.abstract_hr: Riječ je o propovijedi fra Stjepana Brčine održanoj u sklopu Duhovno duhovitih večeri, uoči Svih svetih i Dušnog dana. Polazeći od evanđeoskog odlomka u kojem Isus unatoč prijetnjama nastavlja svoje djelovanje, propovjednik potiče vjernike da ne odustaju od dobrih djela i da se, umjesto o grobu, brinu o tome kako će si osigurati život vječni. Na primjeru pšeničnog zrna objašnjava da čovjek koji se zatvara u sebe i teži samo samoostvarenju ostaje sam i nedovršen, a da se pravi život stječe umiranjem sebi i otvaranjem drugima. Upozorava da sudjelovanje na misi i poznavanje crkvenih stvari nisu jamstvo spasenja jer je potrebno osobno poznavati Isusa. Zaključuje da se valja baviti vlastitim spasenjem umjesto procjenjivanja tuđeg te da je život borba za život vječni, uz suradnju s Božjom milošću.
key_points: Isus se nije povukao pred prijetnjama, nego je nastavio liječiti i naviještati, pa ni vjernici ne bi trebali odustajati od dobrih djela na koja ih Bog potiče, čak ni kad nailaze na otpor.

Umjesto brige o tome kako osigurati grob, koji je u Zagrebu, kako kaže propovjednik, skoro skuplji od stana, svatko bi se trebao brinuti kako si osigurati život vječni, jer to nitko drugi ne može učiniti umjesto njega.
Pšenično zrno koje ne umre ostaje samo. Čovjek koji se okrene sebi i samoostvarenju nije propao, ali ostaje sam, nedovršen i nesretan, dok ga Bog poziva da umire sebi i otvori se drugima.
Riječi 'tko mrzi svoj život na ovome svijetu' ne znače prezir prema životu, nego stupnjevanje: zemaljski život je Božji dar, ali vječni život ima veću vrijednost.
Nije problem nešto imati, nego dopustiti da stvari posjeduju nas. Slobodni smo od onoga što imamo tek ako to možemo davati.
Isus pitanje o tome koliko će se ljudi spasiti okreće prema samim slušateljima, pa se vjernici trebaju baviti vlastitim spasenjem, a ne procjenjivati spasenje drugih.
Ići na misu i pričešćivati se nije jamstvo spasenja. Nije dovoljno znati za Isusa, nego ga treba osobno poznavati, a život je, prema riječima svetog Pavla, borba za život vječni do kraja.
key_topics_en: All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day
dying to oneself and opening up to others
key_points_en: Jesus did not retreat before threats, but continued to heal and proclaim, so believers too should not give up on the good deeds to which God prompts them, even when encountering resistance.

Instead of worrying about how to secure a grave, which in Zagreb, as the preacher says, is almost more expensive than an apartment, everyone should care about how to secure eternal life for themselves, because no one else can do that in their place.

A grain of wheat that does not die remains alone. A person who turns to oneself and self-actualization is not ruined, but remains alone, incomplete, and unhappy, while God calls them to die to oneself and open up to others.
The words 'whoever hates his life in this world' do not mean contempt for life, but a gradation: earthly life is God's gift, but eternal life has greater value.
Having something is not the problem, but rather allowing things to possess us. We are free from what we have only if we are able to give it away.

Jesus turns the question about how many people will be saved back toward the listeners themselves, so believers should concern themselves with their own salvation, rather than judging the salvation of others.

Going to Mass and receiving communion is not a guarantee of salvation. It is not enough to know about Jesus, but one must know Him personally, and life is, in the words of Saint Paul, a fight for eternal life until the end.
summary.title_en: [DDV HOMILY] Is Going to Mass Enough to Be Saved? - fra Stjepan Brčina
summary.abstract_en: This is a homily by fra Stjepan Brčina delivered as part of the Duhovno-duhovite večeri, on the eve of All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day. Starting from the Gospel passage in which Jesus, despite threats, continues His activity, the preacher encourages believers not to give up on good deeds and, instead of worrying about a grave, to care about how they will secure eternal life for themselves. Using the example of the grain of wheat, he explains that a person who closes in on oneself and strives only for self-actualization remains alone and incomplete, while true life is gained by dying to oneself and opening up to others. He warns that participating in Mass and knowing Church matters are not a guarantee of salvation because it is necessary to know Jesus personally. He concludes that one should concern oneself with one's own salvation instead of judging that of others, and that life is a fight for eternal life, in cooperation with God's grace.
